title: scaffold reforrest project with gunshi-style CLI
description:
## Overview

Scaffold a new Rust project for `reforrest` as a separate crate, using `gunshi`-style CLI conventions. This is a prerequisite workspace setup ticket before implementing the actual push logic.

## What it does

- Create a new crate (e.g. `reforrest/` directory or workspace member) in the is-tree workspace.
- Wire up `clap` derive CLI with initial subcommand structure:
  - `reforrest push [path]` — discover and push trees
  - `reforrest status [path]` — show what would be pushed (dry-run default)
  - `reforrest ensure-remote [path]` — create missing remotes via forge CLIs
- Depend on `is-tree` as a library crate for tree detection/classification.
- Basic `--dry-run`, `--json`, `--verbose` flags wired but not yet functional.
- Skeleton `main.rs` with subcommand dispatch.

## Key considerations

- May require splitting is-tree into a lib+bin crate so reforrest can import detection logic.
- Follow existing workspace conventions (Cargo.toml workspace, clap derive, tokio async).

## Dependencies

- This is a dependency of is-tree-reforrest-cli (the epic).

title: reforrest: replicate local git and jj states to remotes
description:
## Overview

Create a `reforrest` CLI tool (Rust binary in this workspace) that discovers all local git/jj trees using is-tree's detection logic and pushes their local state up to tracked remotes — effectively "making the trees flow out to far places."

## What it does

Given a root directory (e.g. `~/src`), `reforrest`:

1. **Discovers** all git and jj repositories/worktrees beneath the given path (leveraging is-tree's existing classification logic for `git`, `jj`, `worktree-git`, `worktree-jj`).
2. **Inspects** each tree's local state relative to its tracked remote(s):
   - For jj repos: local bookmarks ahead of remote bookmarks, unpushed changes.
   - For git repos: local branches ahead of remote tracking branches.
3. **Replicates** (pushes) local state up to remotes:
   - `jj git push --all` for jj trees.
   - `git push --all` for git trees.
4. **Reports** a summary of what was pushed, what was skipped (up-to-date), and what failed (e.g. no remote configured, auth issues).

## Architecture

- New binary target `reforrest` in the existing `is-tree` Cargo workspace.
- Reuse is-tree's detection/classification module as a library dependency.
- Async push operations across discovered trees using tokio (already a dep).

## Key considerations

- Should be idempotent — safe to run repeatedly, no-ops when already synced.
- Must handle mixed trees (some jj, some git, some worktrees) gracefully.
- Worktrees: push from the main tree location, skip worktrees to avoid duplicate pushes.
- Error handling: collect per-tree results, don't let one failure stop the rest. Report aggregate at end.
- Respect `.gitignore`-style exclusions or a config for paths to skip.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `reforrest ~/src` discovers all trees, classifies them, and pushes ahead state to remotes
- [ ] Summary output shows pushed / up-to-date / failed / skipped counts per tree
- [ ] Handles jj repos, git repos, and worktrees correctly
- [ ] Worktrees are deduplicated (push happens from main tree only)
- [ ] Individual tree failures don't abort the batch; errors are collected and reported
- [ ] `--dry-run` flag shows what would be pushed without actually pushing
- [ ] `--json` flag for machine-readable output

title: improve staleness views across all projects
description:
## Overview

Create a cohesive "staleness view" for is-tree that helps answer the question: "which of my projects are gathering dust?" This combines and builds on the duration column and per-file stats features into a unified staleness reporting experience.

## What it does

- A `--stale` or `stale` subcommand that produces a staleness-oriented view of all trees.
- Tree-level staleness: overall age since last change/commit, with color coding or indicators (e.g. `●` fresh, `◐` aging, `○` stale).
- Configurable thresholds: `--stale-threshold 30d` marks trees older than 30 days as stale.
- Summary statistics: count of fresh/aging/stale trees, median age, oldest tree.
- Integration with per-file stats: `is-tree --stale --files` to drill into stale trees.
- Sort defaults to age descending (stalest first).

## Key considerations

- Should work well with existing `--filter`, `--sort`, `--format`, `--json` flags.
- Color/styling should be optional (respects `--no-color` or `TERM=dumb`).
- Depends on is-tree-duration-column for age data.
- Optionally depends on is-tree-per-file-stats for drill-down.

## Dependencies

- is-tree-duration-column
- is-tree-per-file-stats (optional, for file-level drill-down)

title: recurse into trees and report per-file stats (age, modified, size)
description:
## Overview

Add a recursive per-file stats mode to is-tree that descends into each tree and reports modification metadata for individual files — enabling granular staleness views like "which files haven't been touched in 6 months."

## What it does

- New flag: `--files` or `--per-file` that makes is-tree recurse into each discovered tree.
- Per-file output columns:
  - `file` — relative path within the tree
  - `modified` — last modification timestamp
  - `age` — duration since last modification (relative time)
  - `size` — file size in bytes
- Respect `.gitignore` / `.jjignore` by default (skip ignored files).
- Option to filter/sort by age threshold: `--older-than 30d`, `--newer-than 1w`.
- Output formats: table (default), JSON (`--json`).

## Key considerations

- Could be expensive on large repos — should stream or batch results.
- May want to limit recursion depth with `--depth`.
- `.git` / `.jj` internal directories should be excluded.
- Useful for identifying dead code, stale configs, abandoned files.
- Feeds into the staleness views ticket (is-tree-staleness-views).

title: add duration/age column showing time since last change
description:
## Overview

Add a `duration` or `age` column to is-tree output that shows how long since each tree's last change — e.g. `2h`, `3d`, `6w`. This gives an at-a-glance view of staleness across all trees.

## What it does

- New column: `age` or `duration` — human-readable relative time since `change-date`.
- Uses the existing `change-date` data already collected per tree.
- Format: compact relative time (`2h`, `3d`, `6w`, `1y`) with configurable granularity.
- Available in `--format` string interpolation: `{age}`, `{duration}`.
- Available in `--json` output.

## Key considerations

- Should default to time since `change-date` but could optionally show time since `commit-date`.
- Relative time formatting should match familiar conventions (like `jj log` relative dates).
- Useful for the staleness views (see is-tree-staleness-views).

title: reforrest: auto-create remotes via tangled.org tn CLI
description:
## Overview

Before `reforrest` can push local state to remotes, the remote repositories need to exist. Add support for invoking the [tangled.org](https://tangled.org) CLI tool (`tn`) to create repositories on the tangled forge when a local tree has no configured remote (or no remote matching a configured preferred forge).

## What it does

- Detects when a discovered tree has no remote pointing to tangled.org (or no remote at all).
- Invokes the `tn` CLI to create the repository on tangled.org.
- Configures the new remote URL in the local tree (e.g. `git remote add origin <url>` or jj equivalent).
- Optionally supports other forges in the future via a pluggable "forge provider" interface.

## Key considerations

- `tn` must be available on PATH; graceful error if missing.
- Should support a `--forge tangled` flag or config default to opt in.
- Idempotent — skip if remote already exists for the target forge.
- May need to handle org/user namespace mapping.
- Should integrate into the `reforrest` pipeline: discover → ensure remotes exist → push.

## Dependencies

- Part of the broader `reforrest` epic (is-tree-reforrest-cli).

title: Add semantic search via opencode run / ACP
description:
Add a semantic search mode to is-tree that lets users describe what they're looking for in natural language and gets back ranked candidate repositories.

## Two-phase approach

**Phase 1 — Candidate discovery:** is-tree enumerates repos as it does today (via `--all`), then feeds the list (directory name + any quick metadata is-tree already has) to an LLM via `opencode run` or ACP. The LLM returns a shortlist of likely matches.

**Phase 2 — Deep context dump:** For each candidate, is-tree gathers the "notable files" (package.json, README.md, Cargo.toml, pyproject.toml, etc.) in a single oneshot — concatenating them into one big payload. This avoids N round-trips per candidate. The combined dump goes back to the LLM for final ranking/reasoning.

is-tree already classifies repos and knows their VCS state; it can trivially locate these notable files per candidate and return them all at once, which is the key enabler for phase 2.

## Open questions

- `opencode run` (one-shot subprocess) vs ACP (persistent connection with conversation context) — run is simpler to start with, ACP may be better for interactive refinement.
- How to structure the prompt for phase 1 (just dir names + metadata?) vs phase 2 (full notable-file dump).
- Whether to stream results or wait for full response.
- Configurable notable-files list (per-language heuristics vs user-supplied glob list).

title: Track beads ticket counts
notes:
Monitor beads data consistency across storage backends.

Metrics to track:
1. issues.jsonl count: wc -l .beads/issues.jsonl
2. dolt database count: cd .beads/dolt/is_tree && dolt sql -q 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM issues'
3. dolt uncommitted changes: cd .beads/dolt/is_tree && dolt status
   - Clean: 'nothing to commit, working tree clean'
   - Dirty: shows staged/unstaged table changes
   - When dirty, dolt count differs from issues.jsonl (after bd export)

Current baseline (2026-03-16):
- issues.jsonl: 22 tickets
- dolt database: 22 tickets  
- dolt uncommitted: clean (in sync)

For is-tree integration: add column showing dolt sync status for beads repos.

notes: Use 'bd config get prefix' to retrieve issue prefix. Requires bd in PATH and beads repo.

title: Chain multiple detection strategies

title: Detect prefix from config.yaml
notes: Parse .beads/config.yaml and read issue-prefix setting if present.

title: Beads prefix detection strategies
notes: Implement multiple strategies for detecting beads issue prefix with fallback chain.

title: Get beads prefix for each project
description: Detect and expose the beads prefix for each project. This would enable is-tree to reference beads tickets in output, correlating repo state with tracked work.
close_reason: Replaced by is-tree-beads-epic with child tickets for individual strategies

title: Add timeouts to remote info fetching
notes: Commands like jj log for ahead detection (src/detect/jj/ahead.rs) have no timeout. Slow/unreachable remotes can hang indefinitely. Need timeout handling for remote operations.

title: --all should affect default output format
notes: Currently --all processes all subdirectories but the default output remains minimal (status + directory). When scanning many repos, the default should likely include more useful columns like ahead/commit-date.

title: Implement basic Git and Jujutsu detection
description: Implemented basic detection logic in src/detect.rs using .jj and .git metadata. Jujutsu worktrees detected by checking if .jj/repo is a file (pointer) vs directory (main). Git worktrees detected by checking if .git is a file (pointer) vs directory (main). Priority: Jujutsu takes precedence over Git. Verified against example directories: compfuzor (git), compfuzor-x (worktree-git), niri-mcp (jj), niri-mcp-x (worktree-jj).

title: Command Options Epic
description: Implement all CLI command options for is-tree including sorting, filtering, formatting, and output options.

title: evaluate and adopt vite-plus toolchain from ~/src/vite-plus
description:
## Overview

Adopt the vite-plus (`vp`) toolchain from the `~/src/vite-plus` project for is-tree's JS/TS-adjacent tooling needs (formatting via `oxfmt`, linting via `oxlint`, etc.). This is relevant if reforrest or is-tree grows any JS tooling, config files, or if we want consistent formatting across the project ecosystem.

## What it does

- Survey `~/src/vite-plus` to understand the `vp` CLI, its capabilities (fmt, lint), and configuration.
- Determine what makes sense to adopt for this project (is-tree/reforrest are Rust, but may have adjacent JS needs).
- Document or configure accordingly.

## Key considerations

- is-tree is primarily Rust — only adopt if there's a concrete JS/TS surface area.
- May become more relevant if reforrest grows plugin/scripting support.

title: reforrest watchman: daemonized proactive sync
description:
## Overview

After the core `reforrest` CLI push tool is built, extend it with a long-running daemon mode that uses filesystem watching (inotify/FSEvents) to proactively detect changes in local git/jj trees and automatically sync them to remotes in near-real-time.

## What it does

- Watches configured source directories (e.g. `~/src`) for filesystem events.
- Detects when new commits are created in any git/jj tree.
- Automatically triggers push operations for trees with new local state.
- Debounces rapid changes (e.g. during a rebase or interactive session) to avoid thrashing.
- Maintains a small state file to track last-synced refs per tree.

## Key considerations

- Must not interfere with ongoing operations (debounce window, lock detection).
- Should gracefully handle trees being added/removed while running.
- Configurable sync interval / debounce window.
- Logging of sync activity for debugging.
- Signal handling for clean shutdown.

## Dependencies

- Requires the core `reforrest` CLI (is-tree-reforrest-cli) to be implemented first — this ticket reuses its discovery and push logic.

title: Add expanded --help with detailed parameter info
description: Implemented expanded --help with detailed information about sort, filter, and format parameters. Used clap's after_long_help to add comprehensive documentation only when --help is used. The -h help remains condensed while --help shows detailed parameter documentation including examples for filter types, sort columns, and format columns.

title: Add json flag for JSON output
description: Implemented --json flag to output results in JSON format as an array of objects with all columns as fields. Uses serde and serde_json libraries for serialization. JSON output includes all columns: status, directory, commit_date, change_date, workparent. When --json is specified, output is JSON array regardless of --format flag.

title: Add workparent flag and column
description: Implemented workparent column showing the directory name of the workparent (without path) for worktrees. For Git worktrees, parses .git file containing gitdir path. For Jujutsu worktrees, reads .jj/repo pointer file. Returns empty string for non-worktree repositories. Supports sorting by workparent column with None values sorted after Some values.

title: Add change-date flag and column
description: Implemented change-date column showing the most recent file change date for each repository. Uses directory metadata to get modification time via std::fs::metadata().modified(). Formats date using chrono library with ISO 8601 format. Supports sorting by change-date column.

title: Add commit-date flag and column
description: Implemented commit-date column showing the most recent commit date for each repository. Uses git log -1 --format=%ci to fetch commit date for both Git and Jujutsu repositories. For Jujutsu worktrees, reads the .jj/repo pointer file to locate the actual git backend. Returns empty string for repositories with no commits. Supports sorting by commit-date column.

title: Add date flag for date format specification
description: Implemented --date flag for specifying date format string. Default format is ISO 8601. The date format string is accepted and stored for use by commit-date and change-date columns when they are implemented in their respective tickets.

title: Add format flag for custom output format
description: Implemented --format flag for custom output format with interpolated columns. Currently supports columns: status, directory. Columns commit-date, change-date, workparent are supported but return empty strings until implemented in their respective tickets. Format string uses {column} syntax for interpolation (e.g., "{status} {directory}").

title: Add --reverse/-R flag for reversing sort order
description: Add --reverse/-R flag to reverse the sort order of results.
close_reason: Removed from spec - reverse functionality replaced with +/- suffixes on sort columns

title: Add sort flag for sorting results
description: Implemented --sort flag for sorting by any column with comma-separated multiple sorts and +/- suffixes for direction. Currently supports sorting by: status, directory. Support for commit-date, change-date, and workparent columns will be added in their respective tickets. Sort specifications are parsed with +/- suffix for ascending/descending, and default to ascending if no suffix.

title: Add filter flag for type filtering
description: Implemented --filter flag with comma-separated filters and - suffix for NOT. Filtering logic: positive filters are OR'd (show if any positive filter matches), negative filters are AND'd (exclude if any negative filter matches). When only negative filters exist, shows all entries except those matching the negative filters. Supports filter types: git, jj, worktree, worktree-git, worktree-jj.

title: Add all/-a flag for testing all directories
description: Implemented --all/-a flag using clap for argument parsing. When --all is specified, recursively scans current directory for subdirectories (excluding hidden directories starting with .) and tests each one. Maintains existing functionality for testing specific directories via positional arguments.
